L31:   * # bias cut
L32: ## 【15†transitive verb】
L33: 
L34: variants or bias-cut
L35: 
L36: bias cut or bias-cut; bias cutting or bias-cutting; bias cuts or bias-cuts
L37: 
L38: : to cut (something) diagonally : to cut (something) on a bias
L39: 
L40: An attractive serving style is to bias-cut each chicken breast half into ¼-inch slices.—Barbara Mundall, Better Homes and Gardens, October 2000
L41: 
L42: Lucilla purchased more fabric and experimented until she got the knack of bias-cutting … printed silk.—Bruce Boyer, Town & Country, June 1990
L43: The stripes shall be sewed on the sleeve 1½ inches above the point of the cuff at an angle of 30 degrees with the bottom of the sleeve and the ends shall be bias cut to show a vertical edge.—United States Marine Corps, Uniform Regulations
L44: 
L45: Slashes should always be bias cut and should never be cut along the grain line; the latter will cause fraying.—Michele Morrow Harer, Big Book of Quilting, 2005
L46: 
L47: bias-cut adjective
L48: Carve the joint in long thin bias-cut fillets, then turn it over and carve from the undercut. —Elizabeth David, French Provincial Cooking, 1999
L49: 
L50: … bias-cut slices of hot sausage … —James Hynes, Kings of Infinite Space, 2005
L51: 
L52: The people are like long, tapering candles, a swarm of tuxedos and bias-cut silks. —Jane Mendelsohn, I was Amelia Earhart, 1996
L53: 
L54: … one of those unforgiving bias-cut dresses … —Charla Krupp, Time, 19 Mar. 2001
